q: Lecture 13 – Intraocular pressure – slide 3: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Aqueous humor formation

  • produced in posterior chamber
  • the epithelium of the ciliary processes
  • active process of secretion (active transport) 75%
  • ultrafiltration. 25%
  • passes through the pupil into anterior chamber
  • metabolic changes with cornea,lens

q: Lecture 13 – Intraocular pressure – slide 4: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Aqueous humor outflow

  • via anterior chamber angle
  • iris root and the cornea
  • elimination
  • mainly outflow
  • Mainly by drainage system within the angle
  • by uveo-scleral and vitreous pathway
  • small by
  • diffusion
  • active transport

q: Lecture 13 – Intraocular pressure – slide 6: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Trabecular tissue (trabeculum)

  • pore-like meshwork
  • grill-like tissue
  • lines anterior chamber angle
  • superposition of lamellae
  • bundles that anastomose to make pores (2-12 microns)
  • the pores of two neighbouring lamellae do not correspond one to another;
  • a system of tortuous canals
  • anterior chamber
  • the inner wall of the Schlemm’s canal

q: Lecture 13 – Intraocular pressure – slide 7: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Schlemm’s canal

  • intralimbally circular channel.
  • afferent limbs
  • tortuous channels within the trabecular tissue.
  • efferent limb
  • 20-30 efferent vessels (aqueous veins)
  • leave the Schlemm’s canal through its external wall;
  • most merge together to form the profound intrascleral plexus;
  • a small penetrate the sclera and eventually end in episcleral venous plexus
  • aqueous humor joins the venous circulation

q: Lecture 13 – Intraocular pressure – slide 8: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Intrascleral plexus

  • richly anastomosed network.
  • vessels from the Schlemm’s canal
  • veins belonging to intraocular venous plexus
  • sends communicating vessels
  • empty out in episcleral venous plexus
  • ends in conjunctival venous plexus
